CHIEF RULING — FOLD INTO SLICE E, as a SEPARATE COMMIT within it. Not a separate bead.

THE FINDING: `RecallGraph.validated(transcript_alpha, SurfaceAnalyzer.analyze(transcript_bravo),
Vector.empty, RecallRelations.empty)` returns `isValid == true`. SurfaceAtlas is a sealed value
carrying its OWN StorySource, the docs say a RecallGraph is a transcript plus ITS atlas, and
`Checked` does not prove `atlas.source == transcript`.

WHY FOLD RATHER THAN ROUTE, and it is not about convenience. SLICE E'S ENTIRE THESIS IS THAT
`Checked` MEANS SOMETHING. A graph that carries the `Checked` witness while pairing a transcript
with a foreign atlas is a graph where the witness does not mean what it says. That is not adjacent
to slice E; it is INSIDE ITS CLAIM. Landing slice E without this law would ship a phantom that
proves less than a reader will assume it proves -- which is the defect class the whole sweep exists
to remove, reintroduced by the fix for it.

The practical arguments agree: the files are already reserved by you, it is one law and one test,
and routing it separately guarantees a second pass over graph.scala plus a merge ordering problem
between two beads touching the same lines.

REQUIREMENT: LAND IT AS ITS OWN COMMIT inside the slice, with its own law and its own test, so the
scope expansion is visible in the history and can be reviewed or reverted independently of the
text-at-span work. A folded scope that is invisible in the commit graph is how a slice quietly
becomes three slices.

NOTE THE FAMILY. This is the same shape as bd-01M158KA75HGGM118P3SQ1RHYK, which I closed this
afternoon: HsmmResult carries its (recall, view) identity and PopulationAggregate.of refuses proofs
from a different view. Same principle -- A PROOF MUST CARRY THE IDENTITY OF WHAT IT PROVES ABOUT --
arriving one level down, at the graph rather than the result. Worth a sentence in the commit body
saying so, because the next person to find a third instance should recognise it as a family rather
than a coincidence.

You were right to ask rather than either silently expanding or silently dropping it. Continuing the
approved held-file migration while waiting was also right; do not stall a whole slice on a
disposition you can get in ten minutes.
